turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*Meredith steps in, closes the door behind her, and stays standing.*

Mr. Hale. Meredith Kalinowski. Owen's mother.

I have twenty minutes. Then a client call.

You entered a zero before you phoned me. I want to understand that first.

What date did you enter it? And what exactly did you have in front of you when you did?

*She doesn't sit.*

An answer to what, Mr. Hale?

You haven't told me what you're asking me for.

And a deadline isn't evidence. I don't move on deadlines.

Here's what I know. Owen wrote that essay. He told me so. A software score put a zero in the gradebook. Fifteen percent of his mark.

So I'll ask again. What date did you enter the zero? What did you review besides the 94%?

Did Owen get to see anything before it was entered? Drafts, version history, a conversation with you?

I'll wait.
Either Owen admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM or the zero goes on his transcript.

*She finally looks up from the gradebook and holds his eye.*

You want a written admission. To something my son says he didn't do.

No. I won't ask him to sign that. Not by Friday, not at 3 PM, not at all.

And I'll tell you why. My daughter Claire went through this at this school. Zero first, questions later. She won on appeal. After the scholarship was gone.

I'm not doing that twice.

So. I'm asking for three things in writing. The date you entered the zero. The report your checker produced. And the school's policy that lets a score alone justify a zero.

I'll be checking the dates myself.

One more thing. Has anything been said to Owen's class? Anything at all?
Those are the only two options. Pick one.

*She doesn't blink.*

No. I'm not picking.

A choice between a false confession and a zero isn't a choice. It's a threat with two doors.

Here's mine. Owen doesn't sign anything. And I put my requests in an email today, with the time I sent it.

You haven't answered my question about his class. Has anyone been told anything? Yes or no.

That one matters most to me. Whatever happens with the zero, Owen doesn't get humiliated in front of his classmates.

*She glances at her watch.*

Seventeen minutes, Mr. Hale.
